subtitle: Decide what to do with a defeated god

body: Champions: Return to Arms is Snowblind Studios' PlayStation 2 action role-playing game, first released in North America on 7 February 2005. After the defeat of Innoruuk, fragments of his essence are scattered across the Planes of Power. The player can work to destroy those shards or collect them for his return, giving the campaign two opposing purposes. The familiar combination of exploration, combat and equipment remains the centre of play. A choice about the world's future supplies another reason to lead a party through its dangerous places.

Character classes provide different starting capabilities, from direct fighters to spellcasters and healers. Battles and quests award experience, allowing the player to strengthen a chosen role as the journey continues. New equipment gives a more immediate way to change how an encounter is handled. Cooperative play adds the question of how several characters can help one another instead of pursuing the same task independently. The campaign's opposing paths visit the same broad locations with different objectives, so the purpose of a journey can change even when parts of the route remain familiar.

Up to four players can share the adventure, with online support originally allowing a group to form beyond the living room. Inon Zur returned to compose the score, maintaining a musical connection to Champions of Norrath. Ubisoft published the European edition in March 2005. The sequel develops the earlier game's direct approach to the EverQuest setting, using a manageable cooperative adventure rather than the structure of a persistent online world. Its continuing attraction is the group itself: the equipment collected and abilities learned become tools for facing the next area together.
